# RIGHTCLICK

> Install an app. Your AI learns what it can do.

RIGHTCLICK is an Apache-2.0 macOS tool (Apple Silicon, macOS 14+) that reflects existing native capability contracts — Services, sharing services, Finder Action extension metadata — into a contextual capability layer for AI clients over MCP and a matching CLI.

## Install

```bash
brew install rossbuckley1990-hash/tap/rightclick
rightclick setup
```

Tap: https://github.com/rossbuckley1990-hash/homebrew-tap
Release: https://github.com/rossbuckley1990-hash/rightclick/releases/tag/v0.1.0

## MCP tools (same engine as CLI)

- context_inspect
- context_actions
- context_explain
- context_run (requires confirmed:true after human confirmation)
- context_run_status
- context_providers

stdio: `rightclick mcp`
Authenticated Streamable HTTP: `rightclick serve` on loopback (prints a bearer; keep private).

## Proof (v0.1)

Ordinary BBEdit installation changed one plain-text query from 36 capabilities (0 third-party) to 41 (5 BBEdit) with zero BBEdit-specific acquisition code. Generic invocation of service:com.barebones.bbedit:openSelectionService produced a document with the exact fixture text. See docs/BBEDIT-PROOF.md.

## Hard limits (do not invent around these)

- Not every installed app exposes a compatible contract.
- NSPerformService returning true means acceptance, not semantic success.
- Yojam acquisition/invocation pass; browser semantic result is a documented limitation (docs/YOJAM-LIMITATION.md).
- Capability engine is frozen for v0.1.
- Execution status is in-process memory only.
